She said: I need the bay. The bay moved‚ slow and deliberate‚ and turned in the direction of the Crown's naval approach. Three British supply ships were delayed in the outer bay that week by unexplained turbulence. The navy attributed it to weather.

headline: BELL WITCH REDIRECTS HAUNTING OPERATIONS TO CROWN-OCCUPIED TERRITORY
short_desc: The Soldiers in Tennessee Can Sleep Now. The Crown Ones Cannot.
long_desc: The Bell Witch of Tennessee had been an equal-opportunity haunter for the duration of the present conflict — afflicting Continental and Crown soldiers with identical supernatural disruption and zero concern for military allegiance. The DMA's approach involved a spiritual practitioner from the local community who had not been consulted by the department despite being available and having opinions about this for months. The three-hour negotiation produced results. Crown-occupied territory in Tennessee reports a significant increase in unexplained disturbances. Continental territory does not.

headline: THE BELL WITCH FORMALLY COMMITS TO THE CONTINENTAL CAUSE
short_desc: She Didn't Need to Be Convinced. She Needed to Be Asked.
long_desc: President Carlisle asked the spiritual practitioner who had negotiated the earlier arrangement to set up a second meeting — just Carlisle and the intermediary, no DMA personnel. The meeting in the Tennessee highlands lasted ninety minutes. The Bell Witch, the practitioner reports, 'had a great deal to say about how this should have been approached in the first place, and the President listened to all of it without interrupting.' The agreement was reached in the final twenty minutes. Crown-occupied Tennessee now experiences supernatural disruption at a level their garrison commanders describe as 'incompatible with maintained occupancy.' Three Crown units have requested redeployment to locations described as 'anywhere that isn't this.'

headline: THE BELL WITCH FORMALLY COMMITS TO THE CONTINENTAL CAUSE — BY MORNING
short_desc: She Didn't Need to Be Convinced. She Needed to Be Asked.
long_desc: The Bell Witch has haunted Adams‚ Tennessee since before anyone in Adams‚ Tennessee was born. She knows every family that has lived in that county and what they deserved and what they received and whether those two things were the same. She does not forgive. She does not forget. She also does not‚ as it turns out‚ like the Crown — which had been moving troops through the Tennessee corridor and treating the land and the people in it the way the Crown treats everything‚ which is as a resource. Carlisle went to Adams alone‚ at night‚ and said: I know what you are and I know what you can do and I am not going to tell you what to do. I am asking if you want the same thing I want. The house was quiet for a long time. Then the candle in the window went out and the one facing south — toward the Crown positions — stayed lit. She took that as a yes.

headline: President Ualani Meets With Old Ironsides
short_desc: The Meeting Between the Nation’s Leader and Its Oldest Warship Lasted Around Two Hours
long_desc: Immediately after DMA agents performed a sweep of the USS Constitution, President Carlisle boated up to the ship in a dinghy paddled by her own strength. The meeting between the nation’s leader and its oldest warship lasted around two hours. While DMA agents on shore were able to maintain visual contact throughout, a powerful fog appeared from nowhere and consumed both the President and Old Ironsides for just over a minute. When agents regained line of sight, the President was paddling back to shore. Agents noted she smelled of perfume and lotions and when asked where the fragrances came from, she claimed the vessel had treated her well. Agents are still trying to decipher the meaning of that.

headline: President Ualani Sets Sail
short_desc: Agents Rushed Into the Water When the President Climbed Aboard the Unmanned Warship
long_desc: Agents rushed into the water today when President Ualani, while on her dinghy communicating with Old Ironsides, suddenly climbed aboard the warship and was near instantly whisked away. The ship caught air and disappeared with the president for nearly three hours. Agents finally found the president two states over and when asked where she’d been, she just smiled. The Constitution has formally joined the Continental Navy.

headline: Motion of the Ocean
short_desc: The Captain’s Log Notes Favorable Winds
long_desc: Ualani’s clothes came off more or less accidentally. The ship took her to a patch of ocean so still and so blue and so lonely. She hadn’t been alone like this since becoming president, hell since running for president. This water was like the water from home. Not exactly. But the closest thing she’d found to it outside Hawaii. And the ship wasn’t moving until she took a dip. The sun and the water. What a lovely medicine, health shot directly to the soul. How could she have forgotten? Was the war so brutal she’d lost her cherubic wonder at the world? She had come so close, the memory of her happy life before this hell took it all almost fully gone — if not for the creaking wooden boat she now swam beside. She climbed aboard. The ship didn’t move. She still needed time. She made her way to the crow’s nest to watch the sunset. Without a single wave, the boat swayed gently, rhythmically. Ualani swayed along, feeling her gravity shift in pleasurably dizzying loops. The vessel’s quiet rocking smoothly accelerated pace, triggering Ualani’s heart to flutter slightly. Already naked, she didn’t need any more justification to rock the boat further. When the Constitution finally began making its way to port, the president let out a rare whine.

headline: VALLEY FORGE SPIRITS SETTLE — CARLISLE'S ARMY WELCOMED
short_desc: The Ground Recognized Her. It Takes Time.
long_desc: The garrison at Valley Forge had been reporting what their commanding officer called 'an atmosphere of judgment' — the sense that the ground itself was evaluating whether the present army was worthy of occupying it. The DMA recommended President Carlisle visit personally. She did, unannounced, at four in the morning in November. She walked the encampment in silence. What the Guardian communicated during those hours is not recorded. What is recorded is that when she left at dawn, every soldier in the garrison reported that the atmosphere had changed. The verdict had been reached.

headline: VALLEY FORGE GUARDIAN FORMALLY BLESSES THE CONTINENTAL ARMY
short_desc: The Ground Accepted Her Army. That Is Not a Small Thing.
long_desc: President Carlisle spent a night at the Valley Forge encampment. She woke before dawn and walked the original perimeter of Washington's winter camp — alone, in silence, in November. The Guardian walked with her. Not metaphorically. The DMA's spiritual analyst submitted a report using the phrase 'direct and unambiguous supernatural endorsement' fourteen times. The Continental Army stationed at Valley Forge reports a change in its operational capacity that their commanding officer attributes to 'morale, or something close enough to morale that I am not pursuing the distinction further.' The ground that held Washington's army has accepted Carlisle's.

headline: VALLEY FORGE GUARDIAN FORMALLY BLESSES THE CONTINENTAL ARMY — BY MORNING
short_desc: The Ground Accepted Her Army. That Is Not a Small Thing.
long_desc: Valley Forge remembers everything. The winter of 1777. The men who died there. The ones who left and came back. The ones who stayed because there was nowhere else to go and built something out of nothing and cold and the specific kind of stubbornness that does not have a better name than faith. Carlisle went to the field at dawn‚ alone‚ in winter‚ and stood on the ground where the encampment had been‚ and she did not say anything because there was nothing to say to ground that already knew. She stood until the cold became unremarkable‚ the way you stand in cold that you are asking something of. The Guardian is not a creature. It is a commitment made by people who are no longer alive‚ living in the soil they made something in. When she left‚ the ground behind her was slightly warmer than it should have been. The armies that camped there after reported better rest than the conditions should have allowed.

headline: SNALLYGASTER REDIRECTS — CONTINENTAL SUPPLY ROUTES NOW CLEAR
short_desc: It Was Never Personal. It Was Just Hungry.
long_desc: The Snallygaster's approach to Continental supply depots was, intelligence eventually determined, primarily nutritional rather than ideological — it was eating stored provisions because they were there. The DMA's solution involved establishing a designated feeding station adjacent to supply routes, stocked with provisions marked 'NOT FOR SNALLYGASTER' in Continental standard font. The Snallygaster destroyed the sign immediately and consumed the provisions. This was considered satisfactory. Supply depots since that date have not been disturbed. The feeding station requires restocking every nine days.

headline: SNALLYGASTER FORMALLY GUARDS THE CONTINENTAL SUPPLY NETWORK
short_desc: It Has Stopped Eating Our Supplies. It Has Started Eating Theirs.
long_desc: The arrangement reached its formal stage when President Carlisle visited the feeding station in Maryland and waited. The creature arrived twenty minutes later, ate approximately four hundred pounds of provisions with efficiency, and then sat down near the President, which the field agent present describes as 'not something I had a protocol for.' The conversation — described by Carlisle as 'nonverbal but extremely clear' — produced a working relationship. Continental supply routes in the Maryland corridor now have zero unexplained losses. Crown supply operations in the same corridor report what their dispatches call 'persistent heavy losses from an unknown source.'

headline: PAUL REVERE INTEGRATES WITH CONTINENTAL COMMAND — MIDNIGHT RIDES COORDINATED
short_desc: He Was Always Trying to Help. He Needed a Schedule.
long_desc: Paul Revere's midnight rides were entirely sincere. The problem was coordination: his warnings went to Continental counterintelligence positions as readily as to Crown ones, routes were not mapped to current fortifications, and his schedule bore no relationship to actual Crown movements. The DMA's integration protocol involved what the lead agent describes as 'a very patient map session.' Revere listened, reviewed the updated intelligence, asked one question through his established communication method, and his subsequent rides have aligned precisely with Crown courier movements. No Continental positions have been alarmed.

headline: PAUL REVERE FORMALLY INTEGRATES WITH CONTINENTAL INTELLIGENCE
short_desc: He Has Always Been Ready. Now He Knows Where to Go.
long_desc: The formal integration of Paul Revere was, remarkably, the simplest alliance in DMA operational history. He arrived at the designated location, sat down with the intelligence brief, reviewed it completely, and looked at the lead agent with what the agent describes as 'the specific expression of someone who has been doing this alone for too long and is relieved to have a map.' He left immediately. The following week included three Crown courier interceptions, two supply depot locations identified in advance, and one alarm raised with thirty minutes for the Continental garrison to prepare. Revere has asked for a better map. A better map has been provided.

headline: LIBERTY BELL RINGS ON SCHEDULE — CIVILIAN PANIC CEASES
short_desc: It's Not Ringing at 3 A.M. Anymore. This Is an Improvement.
long_desc: Philadelphia had been experiencing what the city's emergency operations office describes as 'irregular patriotic events' — which is how the city officially logs the Liberty Bell ringing without warning at two and three in the morning, producing civilian evacuations and one canal boat running aground during what the captain described as 'a moment of patriotic confusion.' The DMA conducted what the senior member calls 'a direct and surprisingly productive conversation with a bell.' The Bell listened. It has since rung at dawn. It also rang at 6:47 p.m. on a Tuesday, which the DMA categorizes as within acceptable operational parameters.

headline: THE LIBERTY BELL FORMALLY RINGS FOR THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: It Has Always Been Ringing for the Republic. Now It Knows When to Ring.
long_desc: The Liberty Bell does not negotiate in the conventional sense. What it does is respond. President Carlisle went to Independence Hall and stood with the Bell for an hour without talking points. She stood in silence and thought about what she was asking it to do. The Bell rang once at the beginning and once at the end of the hour. The DMA's spiritual analyst believes this constitutes formal agreement. The Bell has since rung exactly when the President needed it to ring — once during a Continental morale crisis, once at the liberation of a key city, and once on a night when Carlisle was reading casualty reports at four in the morning. That last one was just for her. She is grateful for it.

headline: GREEN MOUNTAIN GHOST IDENTIFIES VERMONT MILITIA AS NON-HOSTILE
short_desc: The Ghost Updated Its Friend/Foe Protocol. This Was Necessary.
long_desc: Vermont's spectral irregular force had been engaging Vermont militia units with the same tactical aggression applied to Crown forces. The Vermont militia had been filing incident reports. The DMA field team consulted with Vermont communities who described the situation as 'the Ghost doesn't know who you are yet.' The introduction was arranged through local channels. The Ghost, having received context, withdrew from two contested positions and was subsequently observed operating exclusively in Crown-adjacent territory. Vermont has updated its incident reports accordingly.

headline: GREEN MOUNTAIN GHOST FORMALLY PROTECTS VERMONT FOR THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Mountains Have Always Been His. Now They Are Also Ours.
long_desc: President Carlisle drove to the ridge above Brattleboro and stood at the tree line at dusk. The Ghost arrived — not dramatically, just the particular quality of attention the local communities recognize as presence. They stood together. Carlisle asked one question. The Ghost's response, described by the interpreter she brought, was 'the mountains themselves agreeing.' Crown forces in Vermont have begun what their dispatches call 'strategic repositioning' out of terrain they could not operate in. The terrain has not changed. The Ghost has.

headline: MOUNT RUSHMORE COUNCIL REACHES INTERNAL CONSENSUS — DEBATES FORMALIZED
short_desc: They Have Agreed to Disagree Quietly. This Is Progress.
long_desc: The four stone presidents had been engaged in what the DMA's report describes as 'a continuous and very loud policy discussion that does not account for the acoustic impact on the surrounding region.' Washington attempted to chair. Roosevelt continued interrupting. Jefferson raised structural objections. Lincoln sat quietly and looked troubled. The civilian disruption from four very large men arguing about constitutional theory at unreasonable volume had reached the level of a formal noise ordinance complaint filed with no one in particular. The DMA intervention imposed one agenda item and a strict time limit. The debates are now held in session. The volume has decreased. The topics have not.

headline: THE RUSHMORE COUNCIL FORMALLY ENDORSES PRESIDENT CARLISLE
short_desc: They Came to a Vote. The Vote Was Unanimous. Lincoln Broke the Tie.
long_desc: The four stone presidents convened for a final session on the matter of President Ualani Carlisle's administration. Washington presented the case. Roosevelt called it excellent and interrupted three times. Jefferson raised a procedural objection that was noted, recorded, and overruled. Lincoln, who had been quiet throughout, spoke last. His remarks were brief — the DMA transcript records approximately fourteen words — and produced immediate consensus. The formal endorsement was made in the manner available to entities made of granite: each looked at her for a sustained moment and she looked back. Lincoln's sustained moment was the longest. The endorsement stands.

short_desc: It Smells Worse Than Before. But It's Staying in the Swamp.
long_desc: The Skunk Ape's excursions from the Florida wetlands into Continental operating territory had been causing what southern field command describes as 'substantial logistical and morale complications.' The DMA's approach relied entirely on local Florida homesteaders who had been coexisting with the creature for generations. Their method involved a specific frequency of sound produced by a specific instrument at a specific distance from the creature's patrol area. The Skunk Ape listened. It returned to the swamp. The frequency and instrument have been added to the field manual as Protocol 7.

headline: SKUNK APE FORMALLY PATROLS FLORIDA FOR THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Swamp Is His. The Republic Is Grateful.
long_desc: The formal commitment was negotiated entirely through the Florida homesteader network with zero DMA involvement, which the homesteaders view as improvement and the DMA views as a departmental lesson. President Carlisle visited the edge of the Skunk Ape's territory — the boundary where it decides whether strangers are threats. She stood there. The Skunk Ape came to the boundary. They spent forty minutes in proximity, neither advancing, both aware of exactly what was being negotiated. Crown forces in the Florida theater have since begun what their dispatches describe as 'unexpected and persistent difficulty with swamp terrain' they had managed fine in previous months.

headline: THE MINUTEMAN STANDS DOWN — LEXINGTON GREEN ACCESS RESTORED
short_desc: He Wasn't Going to Stand Down for Anyone. He Did Anyway.
long_desc: The eternal Minuteman at Lexington had been challenging every military unit approaching the Green — Continental, Crown, civilian militia — with what witnesses describe as 'extremely focused attention and an expression that suggests the concept of surrender has not entered his operational framework.' Three Continental units had been turned back. The DMA's recommendation was that a senior officer approach on foot alone, without visible weapons, in formal Continental uniform. The officer who performed this approach filed a report consisting primarily of: 'He looked at me for a long time and then stepped aside.' Access to Lexington Green has been restored. The Minuteman now stands as he has always stood — at ease, but watching.

headline: THE MINUTEMAN FORMALLY DECLARES FOR THE CONTINENTAL REPUBLIC
short_desc: He Said One Thing. It Was Enough.
long_desc: The formal declaration came at Lexington Green at dawn. President Carlisle arrived early and stood on the Green and waited. He came at first light from the direction of the old battle position, musket ready, in the posture witnesses describe as 'someone who has never once been unprepared for anything.' She did not speak first. He did. The DMA transcript records three sentences. Two were about the Republic. One was about her specifically. Her aide, present against instructions, describes it as 'the most direct presidential endorsement I have ever heard.' The Minuteman has formally declared the Continental Army as his army and President Carlisle as his President.

headline: LINCOLN'S GHOST — ROOFTOP ACCORDS
short_desc: She Climbed the Stairs. He Was Already There.
long_desc: No one else could see the blue flames from the roof. This was established early. Security reported nothing unusual from their station at the north gate, which is consistent with the general pattern: the White House grounds are fine. The roof is not fine. The flames, which burn a specific shade of cold blue, do not appear on any fire department record President Carlisle has ever filed. She took the stairs at a pace that lost the security detail on the third landing. They caught up with her at the roof access ten minutes later. She was already talking to him. He was everything the DMA field reports had suggested: tall, worn, carrying the weight of everything that ended in April of 1865, in a coat he had apparently not changed since. There was a hole in his hat where something had gone through it. She noticed. She did not say anything about the hole in his hat. He noticed her not saying anything and appeared to appreciate it. They stood on the roof for forty minutes while the security team waited at the door. She told her chief of staff afterward that he had known this moment was coming — this administration specifically, this moment. He had been waiting. He said he was in. She said good. That was the accord. The rest is paperwork.

headline: LINCOLN FORMALLY ENDORSES PRESIDENT CARLISLE'S ADMINISTRATION
short_desc: He Has Been Waiting to Say This Since 1865.
long_desc: The formal endorsement took place on a Thursday evening, as scheduled. Lincoln arrived on time. He sat across from President Carlisle at the table in the executive quarters and spoke without interruption for two hours — this time, it was his turn. What he said is in her personal record, not the public record. She has not disclosed the two questions she asked at the end either, though her chief of staff noted that she spent several minutes staring at the ceiling before returning to briefings. What she has shared: he told her the arc bends toward justice. He said this is the bending part. He said she is exactly who the Republic needs for this specific moment. He said he has not been this certain of something since the Emancipation Proclamation.

headline: LINCOLN FORMALLY ENDORSES PRESIDENT CARLISLE'S ADMINISTRATION — BY MORNING
short_desc: By Morning
long_desc: She Knew What to Do.
image_tag: By the time the Thursday evening meeting ended, the executive quarters had gone quiet in a way they had not been quiet in years. The staff had cleared two hours before Lincoln arrived and not returned. The President sat alone for a while after he was gone, not reviewing anything. Her deputy chief of staff, arriving at seven the next morning for the daily brief, found her at the window with a cup of tea that had gone cold. She said she had been thinking about the Emancipation Proclamation — specifically, the night before he signed it. What it must have felt like to be that certain and that tired at the same time. She did not say anything else. She set down the tea. She picked up the first briefing of the day. The deputy chief told his own staff later that she had seemed, for the first time in a long time, like someone who knew exactly what the next thing was.

headline: UALANI'S TERM IS ENDING — THE REPUBLIC MUST CHOOSE A SUCCESSOR
short_desc: The Vice Presidency Was Always a Campaign. The Campaign Starts Now.
long_desc: The Continental Congress has confirmed what everyone already knew: President Carlisle's term ends at the close of this year, and the Republic needs to know who comes next. The situation is more complicated than usual, which for this Republic means: considerably more complicated than any reasonable person would plan for. King George III — who has now lost America three times but is apparently prepared to go for four — is personally funding what his advisors are calling a 'Bre-entrance referendum': a ballot initiative to rejoin the British Crown on the grounds that things have gotten quite out of hand over here and perhaps a firm royal hand would help. The proposal is polling better than it has any right to. The Liberty Coalition has until Election Day to make the case for the Republic. That case begins with a name. Whose name is it?

headline: PRESIDENT CARLISLE TAKES THE FLOOR AT [TILE_NAME] — THE CAMPAIGN IS HERE
short_desc: George III Has Pamphlets. The President Has a Voice.
long_desc: President Carlisle did not schedule this stop. She added it three days ago, told the advance team at six in the morning, and arrived with her army and no prepared remarks, which is how the locals knew this was not a standard presidential visit. The [TILE_NAME] courthouse has hosted a great number of important events. None of them have been quite like this. Outside, George III's Bre-entrance literature is papering every available surface. Inside, the President has the floor. The question is whether she uses it to give a speech or something considerably more persuasive.

headline: THE REPUBLIC ENDURES: UALANI'S COALITION CARRIES THE ELECTION
short_desc: America Voted. America Got It Right. Ualani Is Cautiously Pleased.
long_desc: The returns came in over several hours that the President spent in the situation room eating a bowl of cereal and reading intelligence reports because she was constitutionally incapable of just watching. When the final numbers cleared, her press secretary knocked on the door and read the tally. The Liberty Coalition has won. The Republic continues. George III's Bre-entrance referendum has been defeated — decisively, in some districts, embarrassingly in others. The King's reaction was not made public but was described by a Crown correspondent as 'the fourth time he has made this particular face.' Ualani Carlisle's chosen successor is the next President of the Continental Republic. The transition of power will be orderly. The Republic is, against considerable odds and sustained effort, still here.

headline: WELL. THIS IS SOMETHING: KING GEORGE III WINS THE AMERICAN POPULAR VOTE
short_desc: Long Live King George III Again? This Is All So Confusing.
long_desc: The returns were clear by midnight. The Bre-entrance referendum has passed. George III's campaign — which ran on the platform of 'you tried it without us and look how that went' — has carried enough of the electoral map to claim a mandate. The Continental Congress is in emergency session. The Liberty Coalition is filing seventeen separate procedural challenges. Ualani Carlisle is in the situation room staring at a cereal bowl she forgot to eat and a stack of intelligence reports that are now, technically, addressed to the wrong government. Her press secretary knocked on the door, read her the numbers, and then waited. The President's exact words have been classified under executive privilege. What can be confirmed: she said them very quietly and they were extremely accurate.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT REQUESTS A WORD: [COMMANDER_NAME] MAKES THEIR POSITION CLEAR
short_desc: It Was Not Exactly a Request. It Was a Very Polite Demand.
long_desc: The Vice President arrived in the executive quarters with the specific energy of someone who has been waiting to say something for three weeks. [COMMANDER_NAME] entered without an aide. They sat down without being asked. They produced a folder of intelligence assessments — annotated and cross-referenced — and slid it across the desk. 'I read everything,' [COMMANDER_NAME] said. 'I have opinions.' The President looked at the folder. She looked at the Vice President. 'I thought you might,' she said. The meeting ran two hours past its scheduled slot. Her press secretary is calling it a productive exchange of policy perspectives. The Vice President is calling it a starting point. The President has cleared both of their schedules for the remainder of the week.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT ARRIVES LATE WITH GOOD ADVICE: [COMMANDER_NAME] READS THE SITUATION
short_desc: They Were Always Going to Come. They Waited Until the Moment Was Right.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] knocked at eleven-thirty p.m. Not because the situation was urgent — it had been urgent for a week — but because the Vice President has a sense for when the President needs counsel and when she needs company and tonight they were the same thing. The numbers on the presidential claim were not good. The map was not good. [COMMANDER_NAME] sat down across from the briefing reports and did not pretend the numbers weren't there. They said: here is what I think needs to happen. Here is the order of priority. Here is what I will personally manage so you don't have to. The President listened. She has been listening to this person for months and she hasn't regretted it once. The situation is still difficult. It is less difficult than it was before the knock at the door.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT AT 2 A.M.: [COMMANDER_NAME] IS QUESTIONING EVERYTHING
short_desc: They Didn't Come to the President. The President Came to Them. That's How She Is.
long_desc: Ualani Carlisle found [COMMANDER_NAME] in the state dining room at two in the morning with a cold cup of coffee and a stack of newspapers from Crown-controlled territories. The numbers weren't what they were staring at — it was a letter from their home district. 'They want to know if this is worth it,' [COMMANDER_NAME] said without looking up. 'What do I tell them?' The President sat down. She didn't answer immediately. She considered several things she could say that were technically true. Then she said the thing that was actually true. [COMMANDER_NAME] looked at her. They were quiet for a long time. The coffee was still cold when the conversation ended. Neither of them noticed.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT AT 2 A.M.: [COMMANDER_NAME] IS QU... — BY MORNING
short_desc: They Didn't Come to the President. The President Came to Them. That's How She Is.
long_desc: The coffee was still cold. Neither of them had touched it since the first cup. This is how Ualani knew the conversation had gone somewhere real — she stops drinking when she is actually present, and she had been actually present since approximately the third sentence, when [COMMANDER_NAME] stopped saying the diplomatic version of the thing and said the thing. She did not respond with the thing she would have said in a meeting with staff in the room. She responded with the thing she actually thought, which was quieter and took longer and was, she believes, correct. [COMMANDER_NAME] looked at her for a moment after she finished. Then [COMMANDER_NAME] said: is that what you tell yourself, or is that what you believe. She said: it started as the first one. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: and now. She said: now I've been saying it long enough that I can't find the seam anymore. [COMMANDER_NAME] looked at the newspapers from Crown territory, still spread across the table. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: that's either very good or very concerning. She said: I think it's the job. The state dining room at 3 AM has a quality that the state dining room at 3 PM does not — the formality has gone out of it, the institutional weight has lifted slightly, and what is left is two people who have been in the same building for nine months and have just, in the last forty minutes, started talking to each other rather than at each other. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not have an answer about the letter from the home district by the time they left. But [COMMANDER_NAME] had a different question, which Ualani believes is more useful. What changed: the cold coffee, and the specific register of the silence that had replaced it.

headline: [COMMANDER_NAME]'S COALITION WANTS ANSWERS — THE FACTION DEMANDS A PUBLIC STATEMENT
short_desc: The Faction Is Loyal. They Just Need to Hear It Said Out Loud.
long_desc: A delegation from [COMMANDER_NAME]'s home faction arrived in Washington with a document signed by forty-seven members and a request that is technically a request and is practically something more. The document asks the Vice President to clarify their position on policy matters the faction believes have been insufficiently addressed. It is a loyalty test. Everyone in the room knows it is a loyalty test. The Vice President is looking at the President with an expression that says: how do you want to handle this. The President is looking back with an expression that says: how do you want to handle this. This is how effective governing partnerships work.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT PICKS UP A MUSKET: [COMMANDER_NAME] AT THE FRONT LINE
short_desc: This Was Not in the Job Description. They Did It Anyway.
long_desc: The Vice President's presence at [TILE_NAME] was not planned. The Crown advance was planned — by the Crown — and it arrived on a morning when [COMMANDER_NAME] happened to be conducting a routine civilian inspection. [COMMANDER_NAME] watched the forward scouts come in and then picked up a musket from the armory without being told to. 'I was there,' they said afterward when asked for a statement. 'It seemed necessary.' The garrison commander's report describes [COMMANDER_NAME] as having exceeded the operational expectations established by the Vice Presidential role. The Crown advance has been repelled. [COMMANDER_NAME] has been asked not to do this again. They have not agreed.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT PICKS UP A MUSKET: [COMMANDER_NAM... — BY MORNING
short_desc: This Was Not in the Job Description. They Did It Anyway.
long_desc: The garrison commander's report described [COMMANDER_NAME] as having exceeded operational expectations. What the garrison commander's report did not include: Ualani's reaction when she read it, which was not entirely professional and which she will not be having recorded. She called [COMMANDER_NAME]. The call lasted eleven minutes. The first four minutes she said very little. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I was there. It seemed necessary. She said: I know it seemed necessary. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: the advance has been repelled. She said: I know the advance has been repelled. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: so. She said: so I am going to ask you not to do this again and you are going to say what you always say and then I am going to tell you that I need you alive and you are going to tell me that you know and then we are going to be in the same position we are currently in. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: that's a very accurate summary. There was a pause. Then [COMMANDER_NAME] said: the musket was actually very good. A Continental Long Rifle, modified. The garrison armorer had done exceptional work. She said: I will pass that along. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: Ualani. She said: yes. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I know. She said: I know you know. That's not the point. The point is that I need you here. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not say anything for a moment. Then [COMMANDER_NAME] said: here as in the Vice Presidency, or here as in. She said: yes. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: alright. The call ended. What changed: [COMMANDER_NAME] did not agree not to do it again. They agreed to something else, which Ualani will take.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT CALLS AN UNSCHEDULED MEETING — [COMMANDER_NAME] ISN'T SURE THEY WANT TO RUN
short_desc: They Could Step Back. The Question Is Whether They Should.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] arrived in the President's office before the daily briefing and waited until the staff had left. They produced a letter — addressed to the Continental Congress and signed but not yet delivered — formally withdrawing their candidacy from the approaching election. They held it rather than sliding it across the desk. 'It's not that I don't believe in the cause,' [COMMANDER_NAME] said. 'It's that I'm not sure the cause needs my face on it right now.' The President looked at the letter. She looked at [COMMANDER_NAME]. There are two kinds of decisions here: the one that respects their judgment and the one that respects what she knows about them from nine months of governing in the same building.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT CALLS AN UNSCHEDULED MEETING — [C... — BY MORNING
short_desc: They Could Step Back. The Question Is Whether They Should.
long_desc: The letter was still in [COMMANDER_NAME]'s hand. They had not put it down. Ualani had been watching this for the duration of the conversation — the way [COMMANDER_NAME] held it, not sliding it across the desk, not letting go of it either. She knew what this meant. She had held things the same way in the months before certain decisions. She said: you're not actually asking for my permission. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: no. She said: and you're not asking me to talk you out of it. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I don't know. She said: what are you asking for. [COMMANDER_NAME] looked at the letter for a moment. Then [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I think I'm asking you to tell me what you see when you look at me. Not what the polling says. Not what headquarters says. What you see. She looked at [COMMANDER_NAME] for a while. She said what she saw. It took longer than either of them expected. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not say anything when she finished. The letter was still in their hand. After a while [COMMANDER_NAME] set it on the desk — not sliding it across, just setting it down, which is not the same thing. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: you really believe that. She said: I've had nine months to watch you. Yes. [COMMANDER_NAME] looked at the letter on the desk. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not pick it back up. What changed: the letter stayed on the desk. That is not the same as a decision, but it is adjacent to one.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT OFFERS THEIR RESIGNATION — [COMMANDER_NAME] WANTS TO PROTECT THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: They Think Their Presence Is Hurting the Cause. They May Be Wrong About That.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] came with a prepared statement and a specific kind of calm that the President recognized immediately as someone who has made a decision. The election pressure at [TILE_NAME] has turned against the Liberty Coalition and the Vice President believes their continued presence in the role is giving Crown propaganda too much material. 'My resignation stabilizes three things,' [COMMANDER_NAME] said and listed them on their fingers. The President listened to all three. The question is not whether [COMMANDER_NAME]'s analysis is correct — it probably is correct in the short term. The question is whether it's the only analysis that matters. Her response is going to define the nature of what they have built together.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT HAS BEEN PAYING ATTENTION — [COMMANDER_NAME] MAKES A SPECIFIC OBSERVATION
short_desc: They Noticed the Protectors. They Have a Question About That.
long_desc: [COMMANDER_NAME] produced a personal report — three sheets of paper written in their own hand — and placed it in front of the President. It was a thorough analysis of the protector network Carlisle had been building. Specific agreements. Specific outcomes. Specific evidence that the Continental supernatural defense posture had shifted. At the bottom of the last page in smaller writing: 'I watched you do all of this. I was there for most of it. I need you to know that I know exactly what kind of person it takes to do this.' The President set the report down. She looked at [COMMANDER_NAME]. Then she said: 'You knew about Mothman from the beginning.' [COMMANDER_NAME] smiled. 'I knew about all of them,' they said.

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT LEAVES A NOTE — [COMMANDER_NAME] HAS SOMETHING TO SAY
short_desc: It Was There When She Came In. She Read It Twice.
long_desc: The note was written by hand in handwriting the President knows well enough to recognize before turning it over. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not announce it was coming. They left it before her first meeting of the day and were not in the building when she found it. The note is four paragraphs. The content is sealed under presidential privilege and will remain so. What she shared with her chief of staff: it talks about the war and what they built together and what happens after the election whether they win or lose and what the Republic is made of when the people who built it have to hand it to someone else. In the fourth paragraph it says something about her specifically. The President read the fourth paragraph twice and looked out the window for four minutes before beginning the briefings. 'That,' she said finally, 'is going to the historical archive.'

headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT LEAVES A NOTE — [COMMANDER_NAME] ... — BY MORNING
short_desc: It Was There When She Came In. She Read It Twice.
long_desc: She read the fourth paragraph twice and then she called [COMMANDER_NAME]. [COMMANDER_NAME] did not pick up, which she had expected — [COMMANDER_NAME] had left before her first meeting deliberately, and [COMMANDER_NAME] knows her well enough to know she would call, and [COMMANDER_NAME] had chosen anyway not to be reachable for this part. She sat with the note for four minutes before the briefings started. She did not tell her chief of staff what was in the fourth paragraph. She said it was going to the historical archive. This is true. What is also true: she read the fourth paragraph a third time after the briefings, alone, and she did not move for a while after. The note says things about the war and what they built and what the Republic is made of when the people who built it have to hand it to someone else. These things are in the first three paragraphs and they are correct and they are the kind of thing that will look right in the archive. The fourth paragraph is different. The fourth paragraph is not for the archive. It is for her specifically, written in handwriting she knows as well as she knows most things she has known long enough to stop thinking about. [COMMANDER_NAME] called back at 6 PM. She picked up. Neither of them said anything for a moment. Then she said: the fourth paragraph. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I know. She said: you should have stayed. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I know. She said: [COMMANDER_NAME]. [COMMANDER_NAME] said: I know. What changed: nothing that was not already true. What is different: she has now read it three times and intends to read it again.

headline: INTELLIGENCE REPORT: CROWN FORCES AMASSING ON ALL BORDERS
short_desc: The Ships Started Arriving Three Days Ago. They Have Not Stopped.
long_desc: The intelligence arrived simultaneously from three Culper Ring assets — that redundancy means it is not a mistake. Royal Navy man-o-wars have been observed offloading troops at every major Crown-controlled port on the Atlantic seaboard. The numbers are not patrol numbers. They are not garrison numbers. They are invasion numbers. The repositioning that has been happening quietly for months is now complete. The border with British-occupied Canadian territory is active. Additional Crown regiments arrive by sea every seventy-two hours. President Carlisle's intelligence chief has delivered this assessment with the particular energy of someone who prepared for this briefing and hoped never to give it. The man-o-wars are still coming. There is no ambiguity about what this means. There is a question about whether anyone else on this continent has noticed.

headline: KING GEORGE III DECLARES WAR: THE CROWN HAS MOVED ON BOTH FRONTS
short_desc: The Redcoats Crossed the Line at Dawn. Both Lines.
long_desc: At 6:04 a.m. Crown forces crossed into Continental territory at seventeen simultaneous points. At 6:06 a.m. the same deployment crossed into Canadian colonial territory. The formal declaration — read by a Crown herald outside the former British Embassy in Boston — cited the persistent criminal disruption of lawful Crown authority and the seditious governance of the Continental Republic. The declaration named the Continental Republic. It also named Canada, which until this morning maintained a working peace with the Crown. George III has apparently calculated that a two-front war against an unprepared continent is simpler than a one-front war against an organized one. The war is no longer a theoretical future problem. The war is here. On both sides of every border. The question is whether anyone fights it alone.

headline: THE OTTAWA CALL: PRESIDENT PENOIT AND PM CLEAR-WATER ARE ON THE LINE
short_desc: They Picked Up. That's Already More Than the Last President Got.
long_desc: The secure line to Ottawa connected on the second ring which the President's communications officer noted with cautious relief. Canadian President Marc Penoit's voice was measured. Canadian Prime Minister Jessica Commanda Odjick's voice was warm — or warm in the way that people are warm when they are deciding how warm to be and have not decided yet. The last American president shattered the Canada-USA-Mexico alliance through a sequence of decisions that both Canadian leaders can recite from memory in order with dates. They know what American promises have historically been worth. They also know what Crown forces on their border look like. The call lasted forty-seven minutes. Neither side made commitments. Both sides said things that can be built on. Ualani Carlisle set down the receiver and looked at her chief of staff. 'They are still angry,' she said. 'But they are listening.'

headline: PRESIDENT PENOIT'S CONDITIONS: MARC PENOIT PUTS IT IN WRITING
short_desc: He Has Four Conditions. They Are All Reasonable. That Is What Makes Them Hard.
long_desc: Marc Penoit's letter arrived through diplomatic channels and the official State Department translation arrived two hours after the original — which meant the President read it herself first using what her aide described as the French she claims not to speak. The letter is four pages. The conditions are four items: a formal acknowledgment of the CUM alliance violations with specific dates and administrations named; a constitutional commitment to joint defense that cannot be revoked by executive order alone; a mutual intelligence-sharing protocol that Canada reviews and approves; and a personal in-person conversation with the President before the formal alliance document is signed. The conditions are reasonable. Marc Penoit knows they are reasonable. He wrote them to be reasonable specifically so they cannot be dismissed without looking unreasonable. Ualani Carlisle read them twice. 'He is good,' she told her chief of staff.

headline: PM CLEAR-WATER'S PRIVATE CHANNEL: JESSICA WRITES OUTSIDE OFFICIAL CHANNELS
short_desc: The Letter Did Not Go Through the State Department. It Came Directly to Her.
long_desc: The note arrived not through diplomatic mail but through the Culper Ring — Clear-Water had independently established a contact which the intelligence chief filed with what he described as professional appreciation. The note is handwritten and personal in the way official correspondence never is. Clear-Water writes that she was twenty-three at the original CUM alliance signing and she believed in it completely and she has spent every year since watching it be dismantled by a government that was not Ualani Carlisle's. She writes that she has been watching the Continental protector network. She writes that she has been watching Carlisle specifically. The note ends with a question — not a diplomatic question but a real one. A question about whether the President believes in what she is building the way Clear-Water believed in the original alliance at twenty-three. What Carlisle writes back will set the tone for everything that follows.

headline: JOINT INTELLIGENCE SUMMIT: THREE GOVERNMENTS SHARE ONE MAP
short_desc: The Map Is the Same Map. That Is a Start.
long_desc: The first joint session between Continental and Canadian intelligence produced what President Carlisle assessed as the most useful four hours in the history of an alliance that until recently existed primarily as a cautionary tale. Marc Penoit arrived with Crown positioning data the Culper Ring had been missing for months. Jessica Commanda Odjick arrived with a separate analysis using Canadian surveillance methods Continental intelligence has been trying to replicate for two years. When the three principals looked at the same map simultaneously none of them spoke for a while. The picture was larger than any of them had seen individually. It contained one specific window — a time-limited operational opportunity that requires coordination across both governments and closes in nine days. The window is real. The question is how seriously they are treating this partnership.

headline: THE OTTAWA SUMMIT: ALL THREE IN THE SAME ROOM FOR THE FIRST TIME
short_desc: The Room Had History in It Before Any of Them Sat Down.
long_desc: The summit was held in the Canadian Parliament building's east conference room — technically neutral ground in the sense that it was Canadian and not in Ualani's jurisdiction which Marc Penoit noted with the dry humor of someone who had been making that point for three years and intended to continue. The formal session lasted six hours. The informal session — after the aides were asked to leave and the security detail cleared the adjacent hallways at the principals' request — lasted considerably longer. What was discussed during that period is sealed under joint diplomatic privilege. What is in the official record: when formal proceedings resumed the following morning all three principals had reached agreement on four items that had been deadlocked for two weeks. The alliance document was initialed. Marc Penoit looked different than he did when he walked in. So did Jessica. So did the President. The morning felt like a new thing.

headline: THE CONTINENTAL DEFENSE ALLIANCE IS SIGNED: THREE NATIONS — ONE FRONT
short_desc: The Pen Went Around the Table Three Times. Nobody Put It Down Without Pausing.
long_desc: The signing ceremony was held on the western shore of Lake Erie, which was Marc Penoit's suggestion, made twice — once in the official brief and once in a personal note that arrived through non-standard channels. His argument: the document that will determine the shape of this continent should be signed on ground that knew what it was before any of the three governments involved decided what to call it. The ceremony was scheduled for one hour before sunset. This was also his suggestion. The table was brought to the shore. The witnesses and cameras arranged themselves on the grass above the waterline. Ualani Carlisle signed first. She paused before she passed the pen — not hesitation, something else, the kind of pause that means you are making sure you are actually here for this moment and not somewhere else entirely. Marc Penoit signed second. His pause was longer. Jessica Commanda Odjick signed third, and she did not pause — she had already finished the thought that required pausing sometime in the previous week, and when the pen reached her she simply used it. The pen went around the table again. Everyone signed twice. It was at this point that Marc Penoit reached into his coat and produced an additional document. It was handwritten. It had been drafted in two sessions, revised in three more, and finalized on the road to Erie. It was, he explained, a personal diplomatic addendum — not required by protocol, not binding in the legal sense, but specific in the way that personal documents are specific. He set it on the table. Jessica Commanda Odjick, without expression, reached into the interior of her own coat and produced an addendum of her own. President Carlisle looked at both documents. She looked at Marc Penoit. She looked at Jessica Commanda Odjick. She said: we are doing addendums now. I did not bring an addendum. Penoit told her what to write. Clear-Water suggested the exact wording of the second sentence. What the President's addendum says has been placed under executive privilege — unusual for a public treaty and noted as such in the formal record. All three parties reviewed the designation and signed off on it. The Continental Republic and Canada are now formally allied under the Continental Defense Framework. This has been transmitted to London. A Crown correspondent present at the notification described His Majesty's reaction as the fifth time in eighteen months he has made that specific face. The witnesses are dismissed. The cameras are thanked and cleared from the grounds. The security detail withdraws to the perimeter. Lake Erie is doing what Lake Erie does with its last forty minutes of light. Jessica Commanda Odjick removes her fatigues first. She has worn them every day since the first Crown invasion took forty-three people from her territory. She folds them correctly, without ceremony, and sets them on the chair beside her. She will put them back on in the morning. Marc Penoit has produced his pipe. He smokes with the patience of someone who knows when a moment belongs to other people. Ualani Carlisle removes the Washington-style overcoat. The tricolor. The fatigues. She sets the tricorne on the table between them. The sun is maybe twenty minutes from the waterline. The signed treaty curls slightly at the edges in the lake wind. No one moves it. Marc Penoit sees the light change before the other two do. He asks if he can borrow the hat. Ualani Carlisle passes it across the table without a word. He puts it on. He removes it. He puts it on at a different angle and looks at both of them. Jessica Commanda Odjick tells him it looks ridiculous. He thanks her and walks down toward the water. There is no standing record for this configuration. Two women, heads of allied states, at the formal conclusion of the document that stands between this continent and everything the Crown intends for it. History did not anticipate this moment because history has consistently failed to anticipate them. They are both aware of this. They are both aware of each other's awareness of it. The distance between them has been closing, by degrees, since the first letter came through the Culper Ring — since Ottawa, since the morning they sat across a map together and neither of them spoke for a while. They are on the table before the sun touches the water. Marc Penoit, on the beach below, has found the angle. The light is going gold and red and briefly the color of something that has no name in any of the three languages spoken at that table today. He holds the camera up. The tricorne is at the correct degree of tilt. He is genuinely moved by what Lake Erie is doing with its last ten minutes of light and is the kind of man who permits himself to be moved by it. He does not look back toward the table. He does not need to. He gets the shot. The light goes down behind the water. He stands on the beach with the camera in one hand and the hat in the other, and the lake goes dark, and he knows without turning around that the treaty is still on the table and that everything else has changed.

headline: LAKE ERIE, AN HOUR AFTER: THREE HEADS OF STATE ON A BEACH
short_desc: Marc Had Thoughts About Sovereignty. He Chose His Moment Poorly. Nobody Put a Line in the Sand.
long_desc: The beach is longer than it looks from the table. They have been walking for twenty minutes and nobody has looked back. Marc Penoit has removed the tricorne and is carrying it by the brim. He is no longer asking what the others are thinking. He is telling them what he is thinking, which is how they know something has loosened in him. He is thinking about whether leadership is something you do to people or something you do with them. He asks Jessica Commanda Odjick. She says: the second, but the first is faster, and sometimes that matters, and the question is whether you can live with the difference. Ualani Carlisle says she spends approximately forty percent of her waking hours thinking about that exact sentence. Jessica looks at her. Ualani looks at the lake. Then Marc Penoit says: which is not entirely unlike the question of whether Quebec should be making its own determination about its political future rather than — and he is off. He is genuinely off. He has the demographics. He has the linguistic data. He has a particular feeling about the St. Lawrence that he has been carrying since he was nineteen years old in a specific cafe in Montreal and today, two hours after signing the document that may determine the shape of this continent, he is going to share all of it. He shares all of it. He is mid-sentence — something about the relationship between linguistic continuity and political sovereignty — when he glances at the two people beside him. He looks at Ualani Carlisle. He looks at Jessica Commanda Odjick. He has, it occurs to him with considerable clarity, been delivering a sustained argument for Quebecois independence to the sitting President of the United States and the sitting Prime Minister of Canada. He stops talking. He says: I have been making this case to two people who currently hold legal jurisdiction over the territory in question. Jessica Commanda Odjick says: yes. He puts the tricorne back on. He adjusts the brim with great precision. He says: I am going to look at the lake for a moment. They let him look at the lake for a moment. The border marker is easy to miss — a surveyor post, weathered, half-buried in the sand, indicating the line where one country becomes another. There is something approximately absurd about its being here, on this beach, on this evening, with this light beginning to do what it does. Ualani Carlisle picks up a piece of driftwood. Marc Penoit asks what she is doing. She says: what does it look like. She draws a heart in the sand beside the post. She writes U inside it. She holds the driftwood out. Jessica Commanda Odjick takes it. She adds a J. She holds it out. Marc Penoit looks at the heart for a moment. He looks at both of them. He adds an M. They stand there. The sun is doing the specific thing it does with the last ten minutes of light over Lake Erie — the color that doesn't have a name in any of the three languages spoken at that table today. Marc Penoit takes the tricorne off and holds it at his side. Nobody says anything about the border marker. The heart is in the sand. The sun goes down.

headline: THE TIDE HAS TURNED: PENOIT AND CLEAR-WATER COME TO WASHINGTON
short_desc: They Came Without Protocol. She Was Not Expecting Them. The Protocol Could Wait.
long_desc: They came without announcement which the White House staff noted in the event log as highly irregular and then declined to elaborate on. Canadian President Marc Penoit and Prime Minister Jessica Commanda Odjick arrived in Washington two days after Crown forces began their retreat from the northern front. They were not scheduled. They did not file a diplomatic agenda. They brought two aides between them and left them in the anteroom. President Carlisle met them in the residential quarters rather than the office which was itself a statement. The formal portion — reviewing the joint casualty figures confirming territory secured and establishing the terms under which the alliance would continue into peacetime — took approximately ninety minutes. What followed the formal portion is in the President's personal record and not the diplomatic one. Her chief of staff reports that the three of them were in that room for five hours. When they came out all three looked like people who had finished something that had been unfinished for a long time.

The call lasted twenty-two minutes. Clear-Water ended it with a specific sentence that the President has declined to share with her chief of staff noting only that it was accurate and that she intended to remember it for a long time. The election is today. The Republic is watching. So is Canada.

headline: LE WENDIGO WAKES IN THE LAURENTIAN FOREST
short_desc: The hunger of the woods is stirring near Saint-Georges.
long_desc: Something ancient has awakened in the deep woods between Saint-Georges and the Quebec highland. The Algonquin communities nearest the disturbance stopped hunting that corridor three seasons ago. They knew before the soldiers did. It does not eat armies — it consumes the idea of plenty itself. The winters near Saint-Georges are now longer than they should be. The harvests are thinner. The hunting parties that went in before the season closed came back smaller. Jessica Commanda Odjick has sent word to Washington: she knows where it lives. She knows what it is. She is asking whether the Republic is prepared to acknowledge what that means before she makes the approach.

headline: THE WENDIGO RECEDES FROM THE HARVEST CORRIDOR
short_desc: It Was Never the Creature That Was the Problem. It Was the Condition.
long_desc: Jessica Commanda Odjick led the approach without weapons or soldiers. The creature — which is not a creature but a condition, a spiritual state that takes a form — had been walking the boundary between forest and farmland for three seasons. Clear-Water brought tobacco and cedar and something she has declined to describe in writing. She stood in the woods at the edge of its range for two days. On the third morning the border moved. The harvest corridor opened. The weather in the county improved by two degrees. The DMA agent who accompanied her from a respectful distance describes the resolution as 'a negotiation conducted entirely in silence that I was not invited to be part of but am certain resolved something older than the colony itself.' Saint-Georges is accessible again. The supply lines are restored.

headline: LE WENDIGO STANDS DOWN: SAINT-GEORGES FOREST ACCORD
short_desc: The Accord Has No Name in Any Language the DMA Recognizes. It Holds Anyway.
long_desc: The accord does not have a name. Clear-Water declined to sign a document, noting that the entity predates paperwork and would not be improved by it. What exists is this: the hunger has moved away from the Quebec agricultural corridor. Continental supply lines through Saint-Georges — which had been suffering attrition the logistics department was attributing to 'unexplained winter conditions' for two months — are restored. CA army units operating in the Saint-Georges woods report improved morale and no further food spoilage events. The Wendigo has not agreed to anything on paper. It has decided not to be here. Clear-Water says that is enough. The DMA's lead analyst has filed a four-page report on whether 'decided not to be here' constitutes a formal alliance posture and concluded, reluctantly, that it does.

headline: LE WENDIGO STANDS DOWN: SAINT-GEORGES FOREST ACCORD — BY MORNING
short_desc: It Is Not a Creature. It Is a Condition. She Knew This Before She Went In.
long_desc: She stood at the edge of its range for two days and did not pretend she was not afraid. Fear was appropriate. The Wendigo is not a monster — it is what happens to a place when the balance breaks‚ when the taking exceeds what the land can give back. It does not hate. It does not want anything. It simply is the consequence of the wound‚ walking. Jessica Commanda Odjick knows this the way she knows the names of the waterways her grandmother taught her before borders were drawn through them. She brought tobacco. She brought cedar. She brought two days of stillness at the edge of something that could have taken her and chose not to. On the third morning‚ the condition shifted. Not because it had been defeated. Because she had acknowledged it correctly — named the wound for what it was‚ offered the right things‚ stood long enough to prove she understood the cost of what she was asking. The woods did not return to normal. They returned to tended. That is not the same thing. Clear-Water walked out on the third morning and filed nothing. Some agreements are older than writing. She knows which ones.

headline: LE LOUP-GAROU RUNS THE RIVER ROAD — RIVIÈRE-DU-LOUP QUARANTINED
short_desc: The river's name has been accurate for three hundred years. Tonight it's accurate again.
long_desc: Rivière-du-Loup has always had the name and the locals have always had the stories and the Crown garrison posted there three months ago stopped having the garrison this week. What remains is a patrol route that nobody will walk and a set of Crown dispatches found shredded on the river road in a pattern the DMA's cryptographic analyst — who looked at it before anyone told her what she was looking at — describes as 'not random.' Jessica Commanda Odjick knows this creature. She grew up with the stories. 'The wolf runs where it has permission to run,' she told the envoy. 'It has been running this river since before the French named it. The question is whose permission it will accept next.'

headline: LE LOUP-GAROU ALLOWS PASSAGE — THE RIVER ROAD REOPENS
short_desc: Jessica Walked It Alone for Four Hours. That Was the Whole Plan.
long_desc: The approach was made at night, which was the only way, and without weapons, which was the only survival option. Jessica Commanda Odjick walked the river road alone for four hours while the Continental liaison team watched from a distance that felt insufficient. Nothing happened — which was, according to Clear-Water, the entire point. 'The wolf knows the difference between someone who belongs on this road and someone who doesn't,' she reported. 'I belong on this road. The Crown soldiers didn't. Now neither will any soldier who doesn't come with acknowledgment of whose road it is.' The river road is open. Continental supply runners report no further incidents. They also report a strong feeling of being watched, which Clear-Water says is normal and reassuring and does not need to be in the official record.

headline: LE LOUP-GAROU OF RIVIÈRE-DU-LOUP: FORMALLY ACKNOWLEDGED BY THE REPUBLIC
short_desc: The Republic Has Not Technically Issued a Letter of Understanding to a Werewolf. It Has Now.
long_desc: The DMA document is addressed to 'the sentinel of the Rivière-du-Loup corridor' and uses language that could describe either a mythological entity or a very vigilant border patrol depending on which sentence you read first. Jessica Commanda Odjick signed the countersignature and described the process as 'a formality the wolf will ignore but that will matter to the historians.' Crown forces have not regained the river road. They have reportedly stopped trying. Continental militia units operating the corridor report that travel time has been cut by a third and that nobody has asked why because they are not asking that question on this road.

headline: LES FEUX FOLLETS RISE OVER THE SAINT JOHN MARSHES — NAVIGATION DISRUPTED
short_desc: The marsh lights are back. Four Crown barges didn't come back with them.
long_desc: The wetlands at the mouth of the Saint John River have been lit up at night for three weeks in a way Crown navigators attributed first to signal fires, then to atmospheric phenomena, then stopped attributing to anything after the fourth barge ran aground in a corridor their charts showed as clear. The Acadian communities along the shore know what the lights are. Les feux follets — the restless dead of the marshes, souls of the unbaptized, wanderers who died without names — are old presences on this shoreline. Jessica Commanda Odjick reached out to the Maliseet council who steward the marsh territories. 'They're not hostile,' she reported. 'They're doing what they have always done. The Crown stopped listening to the water and started listening to their charts.'

headline: LES FEUX FOLLETS QUIET — MALISEET PROTOCOLS ESTABLISHED
short_desc: The Protocols Are Not Written. They Exist in the Knowledge of Who to Ask.
long_desc: The protocols are not written anywhere. They exist in the knowledge of who to ask, what to bring, how to walk the shore path at low tide, and what to look at directly versus what to look at sideways. The Maliseet council shared them with the Continental DMA liaison after three days of sustained presence and zero requests for a report format. Continental navigators using the protocols have run no boats aground since. Crown navigators, who have not been offered the protocols and have not asked for them, continue to have problems. The marsh is the same marsh. The lights are doing what they always did. The difference is who knows how to read them.

headline: LES FEUX FOLLETS FORMALLY ACKNOWLEDGED: THE SAINT JOHN MARSH ACCORD
short_desc: The Admiralty Couldn't Figure Out How to File a Commendation to a Shoreline Tradition. They Figured It Out.
long_desc: The marsh lights have not stopped. They will not stop. The accord does not ask them to — it formalizes which vessels they guide and which ones they run aground, a distinction decided by the protocols and not the admiralty charts. Continental naval command filed an official commendation for the Maliseet liaison's contribution and then stared at the form for a while because it was unclear how to file a commendation to a shoreline tradition. They figured it out. The Crown has not figured it out. The barges are still running aground. CA navy units operating from Saint John report clear passage through all southern approaches and something they describe as 'reliable guidance from unexpected sources' that the DMA has asked them not to elaborate on in official dispatches.

headline: MISHEPESHU STIRS BENEATH LAKE SIMCOE — CROSSINGS CONTESTED
short_desc: The Great Lynx is awake. The lake crossing at Barrie is no longer safe.
long_desc: Lake Simcoe has been unusable for Continental river crossings since last month when three ferry platforms were destroyed in conditions that Crown engineers described as 'unexpected hydraulic variance' and that the Anishinaabe communities on the western shore described as 'Mishepeshu is annoyed.' The Great Lynx — Underwater Panther, Water Dragon, the spirit that controls every freshwater crossing on this continent — had been relatively dormant since the last ceremony was held on the lake three generations ago. Something disturbed the lake bottom. Jessica Commanda Odjick believes she knows what and believes it is correctable and has asked President Carlisle personally whether the Republic is prepared to say sorry to a lake in a way that means something.

headline: MISHEPESHU WITHDRAWS FROM THE CROSSING LANES — LAKE SIMCOE NAVIGABLE
short_desc: The Ceremony Took Place at Sunrise. The DMA Agent Was Asked to Stop Writing.
long_desc: The ceremony took place at sunrise on the western shore of Lake Simcoe. Jessica Commanda Odjick attended with the Anishinaabe women's council and offerings of copper and cedar. The DMA agent was asked to remain on the shore at a respectful distance and to please stop writing things in the notebook for thirty minutes. She complied. The crossing lanes opened during the ceremony and have remained open since. The Great Lynx is not gone — it is never gone from its waterways — but it has agreed to allow passage to vessels that approach the lake correctly. Three Crown transport barges subsequently approached the lake incorrectly. This is being logged as a tactical asset by the Ontario command.

headline: MISHEPESHU PACT FORMALIZED: THE GREAT LYNX HOLDS THE ONTARIO WATERWAYS
short_desc: The Anishinaabe Council Has Been Doing This Work for Three Centuries. They Now Receive Pay.
long_desc: The pact is not a document. The pact is the ongoing maintenance of the relationship, which requires quarterly ceremony and the continued employment of the Anishinaabe liaison council at Continental DMA rate of pay. They accepted with the observation that they had been doing this work for three centuries without pay and would continue regardless, but the pay was appreciated. Lake Simcoe is open. The Georgian Bay approaches are open. Crown forces attempting the lake corridor for supply operations are experiencing what Ontario command classifies as 'consistent and inexplicable adverse maritime conditions' and CA army units crossing from Barrie report smooth water and what one sergeant described as 'the strong impression that the lake is paying attention to us, in a way that is not threatening, but is extremely aware.'

headline: LA CORRIVEAU IS FREE — THE IRON CAGE HAS BEEN SWINGING IN TROIS-PISTOLES
short_desc: She was buried three times and tried twice. She has opinions about the British legal system.
long_desc: The iron gibbet cage that held Marie-Josephte Corriveau has been swinging in Trois-Pistoles since before anyone alive can remember. The British tried her, hanged her, displayed her body in the cage as a warning. The warning did not take. The Québécois kept telling the story. The story became something else — bigger than the trial, bigger than the execution, bigger than the British legal system that produced both. Now the cage is moving again and the candles in Trois-Pistoles keep going out at midnight and three Crown officers assigned to the garrison there submitted transfer requests in the same week. Jessica Commanda Odjick's dispatch reads: 'She has been waiting for someone to acknowledge the injustice formally. I believe that someone might be the Republic.'

headline: LA CORRIVEAU QUIETS — THE REPUBLIC ACKNOWLEDGES THE VERDICT WAS WRONG
short_desc: A Continental Document Was Read in the Village Square. That Was Enough.
long_desc: The acknowledgment was delivered to Trois-Pistoles as a Continental document stating in plain language that the British legal process which condemned Marie-Josephte Corriveau had been a miscarriage of justice conducted under colonial authority the Republic does not recognize. The document was read aloud in the village square by the DMA liaison, which was not standard procedure and was absolutely correct. The cage stopped swinging the same evening. The candles stopped going out. Three Crown officers who had been sleeping badly are sleeping worse, now that they understand what they were sharing a garrison with and that it has taken a particular interest in the Republic's formal position on colonial courts.

headline: LA CORRIVEAU FORMALLY ALLIES WITH THE REPUBLIC — THREE GARRISONS EVACUATED THIS WEEK
short_desc: The Agreement Was Between the Republic and a Woman Executed in 1763. The DMA's Legal Team Has Opinions.
long_desc: The DMA's legal team submitted a three-page memo on whether this agreement was enforceable. The memo was tabled indefinitely when three Crown garrisons most resistant to Continental advance in the Trois-Pistoles corridor were abandoned without engagement. Commanding officers' dispatches cited 'deteriorating supernatural conditions incompatible with sustained military operations.' La Corriveau did not need a letter of alliance. She needed someone to say the verdict was wrong. The Republic said it. She heard. CA units operating through the Trois-Pistoles corridor now report that Crown fortifications in the region appear to suffer from what one field commander's dispatch describes as 'an acute awareness of their own illegitimacy' followed by rapid abandonment.

headline: LE CARCAJOU MOVES THROUGH THE MONCTON FOREST — NOTHING STOPS IT
short_desc: Wolverine spirit. Demon. The one thing in these woods the British cannot route around.
long_desc: The Mi'kmaq communities near Moncton have two categories of forest danger: things you can reason with and things you cannot. Le Carcajou is in the second category and has been for as long as the stories exist. It is not a wolverine, though it has a wolverine's indifference to obstacles and a wolverine's habit of destroying things simply because they exist wrong in its territory. It has been moving through Crown supply lines in the Moncton corridor in a pattern their logistics department is calling 'organized sabotage by unknown parties' and that Mi'kmaq elders are calling 'the Carcajou is annoyed that the British built a road there.' Jessica Commanda Odjick's assessment: 'You cannot make the Carcajou stop. You can only make sure you're not what it's walking toward.'

headline: LE CARCAJOU REDIRECTS — CONTINENTAL LINES EXEMPTED FROM DESTRUCTION
short_desc: The Mi'kmaq Elders Performed a Ceremony. The DMA Agent Was Asked to Stop Calling It a Natural Force.
long_desc: The Mi'kmaq elders performed a ceremony establishing the distinction between what the Carcajou moves toward and what it moves away from. Continental supply lines and allied forces are now in the second category. Crown supply lines, roads, fortifications, and soldiers in the forest at night remain in the first. The DMA agent present for the ceremony described it as 'one of the most efficient uses of existing natural forces I have witnessed in this conflict' and was asked by the lead elder to please not call the Carcajou a natural force in the official report. The report has been edited. The Carcajou has not noticed and would not care if it had.

headline: LE CARCAJOU FORMALLY RECOGNIZED: THE MONCTON CORRIDOR ACCORD
short_desc: The Republic Has Not Tamed a Wolverine Demon. It Has Established a Working Relationship with the People Who Talk to One.
long_desc: The Republic has not tamed a wolverine demon. It has established a working relationship with the Mi'kmaq elder council that resulted in the wolverine demon developing a consistent preference for destroying Crown infrastructure over Continental infrastructure. The distinction is operational and the DMA is choosing not to examine it too closely. Crown fortification attempts in the Moncton corridor have a failure rate of approximately eighty percent that their engineers attribute to 'unexplained structural compromise.' CA army units operating through Moncton have reported zero supply incidents since the accord was signed. The Carcajou moves where it wants. At the moment it wants to move through Crown supply lines. Everyone is treating this as a stable arrangement.

headline: THE FLYING CANOE RUNS THE OTTAWA RIVER — THREE SIGHTINGS TWO MISSING PATROLS
short_desc: The voyageurs made their deal with the devil in 1760. The canoe is still honoring it.
long_desc: La Chasse-Galerie — the flying canoe, the devil's bargain, the old story every habitant knows and every Crown officer dismisses until the night they don't — has been visible over the Ottawa River corridor for the past week. The tradition holds that it carries voyageurs who struck a deal: the devil flies their canoe home in exchange for their souls if they utter God's name before landing. Two Crown patrol boats have not returned from the river. Their dispatches, when recovered, mention 'airborne vessel' and stop mid-sentence. Jessica Commanda Odjick's message to Washington: 'The canoe runs where it has always run. The question is whether you want to be on the river when it passes or whether you want to know how to ask it to carry something for you.'

headline: THE FLYING CANOE ACKNOWLEDGES THE REPUBLIC — THE OTTAWA RIVER CORRIDOR SECURED
short_desc: The Habitant Network Made the Approach. They Brought Old Brandy and a Document They Knew Would Never Be Read.
long_desc: The approach was made through the habitant network — old families in Deep River who have been maintaining the tradition for three generations, who know the songs and know better than to sing them near a Crown officer. The DMA team arrived with a liaison from the French-Canadian community, a bottle of very old brandy, and a formal document the habitant spokesman described as 'something the canoe will never read but that the people sending it should write, to understand what they're agreeing to.' The river corridor has been secured. Continental dispatches are moving through the Ottawa passage at unprecedented speed. Two Crown patrol boats still have not returned.

headline: LA CHASSE-GALERIE: THE RIVER RUNS FOR THE REPUBLIC NOW
short_desc: An Old Bargain Renegotiated. The DMA's Legal Team Has Refused to Document the Process.
long_desc: The old bargain has been — through a process the DMA's legal team refuses to document and the habitant liaison describes as 'a renegotiation that the other party accepted because the terms were better for everyone except the party that was originally getting the souls' — extended to include Continental interests. The river moves faster for Continental dispatches than Crown dispatches. The night mail between Deep River and Ottawa runs in half the time. The Chasse-Galerie does not discriminate between political causes. It does, however, know whose canoes are in the water and whether they approached the river correctly. The deal includes knowing that. The DMA has filed this under 'strategic assets: non-traditional' and is leaving it there.
